name: Visibility of system status
description: The system should keep users informed about what is going on through appropriate, timely feedback.

name: Match between system and the real world
description: Information, language and conventions should match users' expectations and the world they understand.

name: User control and freedom
description: Users need clear ways to undo, cancel, go back and recover from actions.

name: Consistency and standards
description: Words, controls and behaviours should follow internal consistency and familiar platform conventions.

name: Error prevention
description: The design should prevent likely mistakes before they happen where practical.

name: Recognition rather than recall
description: Users should not have to remember information or hidden rules from one part of an interaction to another.

name: Flexibility and efficiency of use
description: Interfaces should support efficient paths for experienced users while remaining usable for novices.

name: Aesthetic and minimalist design
description: Interfaces should avoid irrelevant information and competition that obscures what matters.

name: Help users recognise, diagnose and recover from errors
description: Error messages should explain the problem in useful language and suggest a path to recovery.

name: Help and documentation
description: When help is needed it should be easy to find, concise and useful to the task.
